topic: Why Ink and Color Were Rejected
questionText:
Read the following excerpt on Somnath Hore's 'Children' and the 'Wounds' series and answer the questions:

Created around 1970 by master sculptor and printmaker Somnath Hore, 'Children' from the celebrated 'Wounds' series is one of the most heartbreaking and ethically uncompromising humanist statements in modern world art. Hore's artistic consciousness was indelibly shaped by his firsthand witness of human agony during the man-made 1943 Bengal Famine and the 1946 Tebhaga peasant uprising. In 'Children', Hore abandoned conventional ink and printing presses entirely, pioneering his radical technique of casting raw, wet paper pulp directly onto a scarred cement matrix. The resulting artwork is an inkless, pure white-on-white relief: the raised paper pulp presents gashes, scars, and skeletal, hollowed contours of starving infants. Hore deliberately refused to use color, asserting that pretty colored inks would only decorative-ize and betray the raw, unadorned tragedy of human suffering, conserved in the NGMA, New Delhi.

Question: Why did Somnath Hore deliberately refuse to apply colored inks to his 'Wounds' paper casts?

options.text: Because he intended to preserve the traditional woodcut aesthetic of Bengal printmaking, which relied strictly on monochrome tonal values.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Because he maintained that wet paper pulp lacked the structural capacity to absorb oil-based pigments without blurring the matrix gashes.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Because he aimed to align with modern Western minimalist printmaking traditions that prohibited bright pigments in relief casting.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Because he believed colored inks would make human agony look decorative, whereas raw white paper revealed suffering in its stark, unadorned truth.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Why Ink and Color Were Rejected.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Modern Trends in Indian Art (Why Ink and Color Were Rejected):
Because he believed colored inks would make human agony look decorative, whereas raw white paper revealed suffering in its stark, unadorned truth.

Detailed Analysis:
Hore refused to turn human pain into pretty decoration; the white-on-white unpigmented pulp forced the viewer to confront the stark, unadorned wound itself. Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

topic: Vulnerability of the Human Figure
questionText:
Read the following excerpt on Anupam Sud's 'Of Walls' and answer the questions that follow:

Executed in 1982 using etching and aquatint on paper, 'Of Walls' by Anupam Sud is a profound psychological and feminist masterpiece of modern Indian printmaking. Sud, who co-founded the pioneering 'Group 8' printmakers' collective in Delhi, is renowned for using the human figure to probe existential themes of social alienation, institutional barriers, and psychological vulnerability. In 'Of Walls', a solitary, partially clad human figure sits on the ground with drawn-up knees, marooned against the colossal expanse of a crumbling, decrepit brick wall. Sud uses the aquatint technique with dazzling virtuosity to build velvety, photographic gradations of charcoal, grey, and shadow, capturing the weathered texture of peeling plaster and exposed bricks. The wall functions as a multi-layered metaphor: it represents the unyielding patriarchal structures, urban isolation, and psychological barriers that trap and alienate the human spirit in modern society, conserved in the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi.

topic: Ganesha by P.V. Jankiram Technique and Materials
questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In 'Ganesha' (1970), P.V. Jankiram crafted a modern linear sculpture using oxidized copper sheet metal, brass wires, and repoussé techniques.
Statement II: P.V. Jankiram carved 'Ganesha' out of a single block of soft sandstone using a chisel.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Ganesha by P.V. Jankiram Technique and Materials.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Modern Trends in Indian Art (Ganesha by P.V. Jankiram Technique and Materials):
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

Detailed Analysis:
Statement I is correct: Jankiram used oxidized copper sheet metal, beaten wire details, and repoussé craft. Statement II is incorrect: he rejected solid carved stone, pioneering modern two-dimensional metal sheet constructivism.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

topic: Key Facets of Krishna Reddy's Whirlpool
questionText:
Match the printmaking aspect in List I with its description in List II:

List I:
(A) Whirlpool (1963)
(B) Viscosity Principle
(C) Multi-Tiered Metal Plate
(D) Hard and Soft Rollers

List II:
(I) Copper or zinc plate etched deeply with acids to create multiple physical relief levels
(II) Hard rollers deposit high-viscosity ink on top surfaces; soft rollers reach deep carved recesses
(III) Masterpiece capturing a dynamic, cosmic aquatic vortex radiating organic cosmic energy
(IV) Physical property where a hard, viscous ink rejects a thinner, more fluid ink applied over it

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

Whirlpool depicts an aquatic cosmic vortex; viscosity principle governs ink repulsion; multi-tiered plate has carved acid levels; rollers of varying hardness deposit inks at different depths.
Hence, Option D is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
